gen-gf-gugi-gf-major-mono-display: Major Mono Display reads like neon tubing, technical and spaced out, with generous sidebearings around every monospace glyph. And Gugi above it stands tall and bold, its lowercase nearly touching the capitals, so the two feel like a loud sign over a quiet readout.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-martian-mono: Gugi's lowercase climbs almost to cap height. Beneath it, Martian Mono lays out loose, fixed-width monospace letters with generous openings, giving the heavy heading a structured, code-like counterpart.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-matemasie: Open and bold on top, closed and tidy below. Matemasie, a sans with broad gaps between glyphs and small entry points into its round letters, keeps a long stretch of text steady against Gugi's flowing, cut-open terminals.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-menbere: Menbere stacks its tall lowercase like rolled cord, a plain sans that stays clean and neutral beneath Gugi's bold display lettering. Paragraphs in it would run smooth and unfussy.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mitr: Gugi draws its strokes at a single constant width, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. It makes a distinctive headline, while Mitr, a contemporary sans-serif with little gap between x-height and cap height, handles approachable text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-momo-trust-display: Distinctive from the first line, Gugi has a blueprint-lettering feel, one constant line carrying tall, open-terminal letters. Momo Trust Display, a clean sans-serif, drifts along beneath with its generous x-height.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mukta: Bold, wire-cut strokes make Gugi feel like lettering bent from a single filament, with open terminals and tall lowercase. And Mukta, a clean sans with tall-bodied small letters, follows quietly; a modest size step down from the heading should be plenty.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mukta-mahee: Mukta Mahee reads chunky and approachable, a sans-serif with tall lowercase letters that fill the line comfortably. Gugi does blueprint-style display lettering best, while Mukta Mahee handles the everyday text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mukta-malar: Gugi's flat, unmodulated stroke weight gives it a bold, distinctive look, with open terminals and tall lowercase. Yet Mukta Malar, a neutral sans-serif with compressed ascenders, makes the strongest partner by simply staying approachable.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mukta-vaani: Gugi feels drawn from smooth wire, bold and open. Mukta Vaani, a contemporary plain sans with a high-waisted lowercase, sits next to it like a quiet colleague beside a loud one.
